name: 3D helicopter stays in budget, the right way up
rationale:
lib/heli3d.lua draws the Rotorflight Configurator's helicopter at any attitude: the
Alignment page uses it, and it is built to be shared by any page that shows a
helicopter. Ethos stops a callback after 20000 Lua instructions, and building the
mesh or computing a frame costs more than that in one go, so the work is split into
wakeup steps and paint only replays a finished list of triangles.

No build and no package step reaches this -- it needs the model built, posed and
drawn against a fake lcd with an instruction-counting hook. The harness keeps every
step and every paint under 12000 instructions through a build, a pose and a rotor
change; pins the orientation the Alignment page relies on (the cw tail rotor right of
the boom seen from behind and the ccw one left; roll > 0 dips the right side, pitch >
0 the nose, as MSP_ATTITUDE gives them); pins what pose() does (hide, lit, a disc
tilt); and keeps paint free of allocation.
